Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 62, verse 5:

The likeness of the Jews, in that they are the bearers of the Torah, its reciters, and its guardians of what it contains, and yet they do not act upon it nor benefit from its verses, although it contains the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the good tidings of him, and they did not believe in him, is that of **the donkey (al-ḥimār) which carries books (asfāran)**, meaning great books of knowledge. It walks with them and understands nothing of them except what passes by its sides and back, namely the toil and the fatigue. Everyone who has knowledge but does not act upon it is like this, and **"how evil is the likeness"** (﴿بِئْسَ مَثَلًا﴾), **"the likeness of the people who denied the signs of Allah"** (﴿مَثَلُ الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾), namely the Jews who denied the signs of Allah that indicate the truth of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ).

The meaning of **"who were charged with the Torah"** (﴿حُمِّلُوا التَّوْرَاةَ﴾) is that they were obligated to know it and to act upon it. **"Then they did not bear it"** (﴿ثُمَّ لَمْ يَحْمِلُوهَا﴾) means they did not act upon it, so it is as though they had not borne it. It has been read as *ḥammalū* (with the emphatic form), meaning they were made to bear it and then did not truly bear it, due to the absence of action. It has also been read as *yaḥmilu al-asfār* (with the verb in the form that does not take the emphatic pattern).

If you say: what is the place (*maḥall*) of **"carrying"** (﴿يَحْمِلُ﴾)? I say: it is in the accusative as a **circumstantial accusative (ḥāl)**, [[Maḥmūd said: "Either his saying *yaḥmilu* is a ḥāl, like his saying:

*And indeed I pass by the base man who abuses me.*"

Aḥmad said: he means that the intended sense here is the category (*jins*), so its being definite and its being indefinite are the same.]] or it is in the genitive as a **qualifying attribute (wasf)**, because the donkey is like the base man in the saying:

*And indeed I pass by the base man who abuses me.* [[The explanation of this line was given earlier in the first part, page 16, so consult it if you wish. End of the editor's note.]]

Hādd Yahūd: idhā tahawwada [[His saying "hāda Yahūd idhā tahawwada" in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: hāda Yahūd: tāba wa-raji'a ilā al-ḥaqq (he repented and returned to the truth), and hāda wa-tahawwada: idhā ṣāra Yahūdiyyan (when he became a Jew). (ʿ)]] awliyāʾu lillāh (the friends of God). They used to say: "We are the sons of God and His beloved." That is: if your claim is true and you are certain of it, then wish for death, that He cause you to die and quickly transport you to the abode of His honor which He prepared for His friends. Then He said: "They will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward" (a reference to their disbelief). The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had said to them: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, none of you will say it except that he will choke on his saliva." So if they had been certain of the truthfulness of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), they would have wished for it. But they knew that if they wished for it, they would die on the spot and the threat would befall them, so not one of them could restrain himself from wishing for it, and this is one of the miracles. It was also read:

"fa-tamannaw al-mawt" with a kasra on the wāw, assimilating it to "law istaṭaʿnā" (if we were able).

(ʿ)]] awliyāʾu lillāh (the friends of God). They used to say: "We are the sons of God and His beloved." That is: if your claim is true and you are certain of it, then wish for death, that He cause you to die and quickly transport you to the abode of His honor which He prepared for His friends. Then He said: "They will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward" (a reference to their disbelief). The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had said to them: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, none of you will say it except that he will choke on his saliva." So if they had been certain of the truthfulness of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), they would have wished for it. But they knew that if they wished for it, they would die on the spot and the threat would befall them, so not one of them could restrain himself from wishing for it, and this is one of the miracles. It was also read:

"fa-tamannaw al-mawt" with a kasra on the wāw, assimilating it to "law istaṭaʿnā" (if we were able).

There is no difference between "lā" and "lan" in that each of them negates the future; however, in "lan" there is an emphasis and intensification that is absent in "lā." So He used the emphatic form once, "wa-lan yatamannawhu" (and they will never wish for it), and once without that form, "wa-lā yatamannawnahu" (and they will not wish for it). Then it was said to them: "Indeed the death from which you flee," and you do not dare to wish for it for fear of being seized by the consequences of your disbelief, "will certainly meet you" and you cannot escape it, "then you will be returned to God," and He will recompense you for what you deserve of punishment.

Zayd ibn ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him) read: "innahu mulāqīkum" (indeed it will meet you). In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: "tafirrūna minhu fa-innahu mulāqīkum," which is clear. As for the reading with the fāʾ, it is because al-ladhī (the one who) includes the meaning of a conditional. And in Zayd's reading, "inna al-mawt alladhī tafirrūna minhu" was treated as a separate sentence, meaning: "Indeed death is the thing from which you flee," and then resumed: "innahu mulāqīkum."

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 62, verse 9–10:

And "Yawm al-Jumu'ah" with a fatḥah on the mīm: the day of the gathering time, like their saying "ḍuḥkah," "lu'nah" and "lu'bah." If you say: What is "min" in His saying "min yawm al-Jumu'ah"?

I say: It is an explanation of "idhā" and a clarification of it. "Al-nidā'" (the call) is the adhān. They said: what is meant by it is the adhān at the time the imam sits on the pulpit. The Messenger of God ﷺ had one muezzin. When he sat on the pulpit, the muezzin would call the adhān at the door of the mosque, and when he descended he would iqāmah for the prayer [[Agreed upon (muttafaq ʿalayh) from the ḥadīth of al-Sā'ib ibn Yazīd, with a different wording, and without "at the door of the mosque."]]. Then Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may God be pleased with them both, continued on that. Then when ʿUthmān came, people increased and dwellings spread apart, so he added another muezzin, and he ordered the first adhān to be given at his house, which was called al-Zawrā'. When he sat on the pulpit, the second muezzin called the adhān, and when he descended he gave the iqāmah for the prayer. No one censured him for that. It is said: the first to name it "Jumu'ah" was Kaʿb ibn Lu'ayy, and it used to be called "al-ʿArūbah." It is also said: the Anṣār said to the Jews, "There is a day on which they gather every seven days, and so do the Christians. Come, let us make for ourselves a day on which we gather, remember God in it, and pray." They said: "Saturday for the Jews, Sunday for the Christians. So make it the day of ʿArūbah." They gathered at Saʿd ibn Zurārah, and he led them in two rakʿahs that day and admonished them. So they named it "the Day of Jumu'ah" because they gathered in it. Then God sent down the verse of Jumu'ah, and so it was the first Jumu'ah that took place in Islam [[Narrated by ʿAbd al-Razzāq from Maʿmar from Ayyūb from Ibn Sīrīn, at length. al-Tha'labī narrated it through his chain. al-Ṭabarānī narrated something similar from the ḥadīth of Kaʿb ibn Mālik, in brief.]]. As for the first Jumu'ah that the Messenger of God ﷺ held, it was that when he arrived in Madīnah as an emigrant, he stopped at Qubā' with the Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, and he remained there on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, and founded their mosque. Then he set out on Friday intending Madīnah, and the Friday prayer overtook him among the Banū Sālim ibn ʿAwf in the bottom of a valley of theirs, so he delivered the khuṭbah and led the Jumu'ah prayer [[Narrated by Ibn Isḥāq in al-Maghāzī from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar from ʿUrwah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUwaym: "some of my people informed me, saying: the Messenger of God ﷺ arrived in Madīnah on Monday," and he mentioned it at length. al-Bayhaqī narrated it through him in al-Dalā'il.

Ibn Hishām mentioned it in his abridgment from Ibn Isḥāq without a chain.]]. And from some of them: God has refuted the claims of the Jews in three respects. They boasted that they were God's friends and beloved, so He refuted them in His saying "then wish for death, if you are truthful" [2:94]. They said they were the People of the Book while the Arabs had no book, so He likened them to a donkey carrying books [62:5]. And (they had) the Sabbath, and that the Muslims had nothing like it, so God prescribed the Jumu'ah for them. And from the Prophet ﷺ: "The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he was admitted to Paradise, on it he was sent down to earth, on it the Hour will come, and it is with God the Day of Increase (yawm al-mazīd)." And from him, peace be upon him: "Gabriel came to me with a white mirror in his palm and said: 'This is Friday, which your Lord presents to you, to be a festival for you and for your community after you. It is the chief of days with us, and we call it the Day of Increase in the Hereafter.'" [[Agreed upon, except for the phrase "and it is with God the Day of Increase." al-Bazzār and al-Ṭabarī narrated it through the chain of Jahḍam ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṭufayl from Abū Ṭaybah from ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmayr from Anas, at length. Its wording is "and we call it in the Hereafter," and this is the correct version. In al-Ṭabarī's narration in his tafsīr of Qāf: "Abū Ṭaybah narrated to me from Muʿāwiyah al-ʿAbsī from ʿUthmān." Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam al-Bannānī and ʿAnbasah ibn Saʿīd, both from ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmayr from Anas. The chain of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam is from Abū Yaʿlā. Ibn Abī Shaybah and Isḥāq narrated it from the narration of Layth ibn Abī Sulaym from ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmayr. al-Shāfiʿī narrated it with a weak chain: he said, "Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Yaḥyā informed me, Mūsā ibn ʿUbaydah narrated to me, Abū al-Azhar Muʿāwiyah ibn Isḥāq ibn Ṭalḥah narrated to me from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmayr that he heard Anas ibn Mālik say something similar." It has another route from Anas narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ, through Thābit ibn Thawbān from Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh from Anas. Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh said: "Muḥammad ibn Shuʿayb informed us, ʿUmar, the client of ʿAmrah, narrated to me from Anas." It has a witness from the ḥadīth of Ḥudhayfah, narrated by al-Bazzār through al-Qāsim ibn Muṭayyib from al-Aʿmash from Abū Wā'il from him.]]. And from him ﷺ: "God, exalted is He, has in every Friday six hundred thousand persons freed from the Fire" [[Narrated by Abū Yaʿlā, al-Bayhaqī in al-Shuʿab, Ibn ʿAdī and Ibn Ḥibbān through Azwar ibn Ghālib from Sulaymān al-Taymī from Thābit from Anas. Al-Azwar: al-Dāraqutnī said, "abandoned" (matrūk). Abū Yaʿlā narrated it through al-Muʿtamir ibn Nāfiʿ from ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿUmarī from Thābit, "Anas narrated to me." It was narrated by al-Bukhārī in al-Tārīkh in the biography of al-Muʿtamir. al-Dāraqutnī narrated it in al-Afrād through ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Zayd ibn Thābit.]]. And from Kaʿb: God has preferred among the cities Mecca, among the months Ramaḍān, and among the days Friday. He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever dies on Friday, God records for him the reward of a martyr and protects him from the trial of the grave" [[ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Ibn Jurayj informed us from a man, from Ibn Shihāb, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever dies on Friday or on the night of Friday, he is protected from the trial of the grave and the reward of a martyr is recorded for him." Abū Murrah said in al-Sunan: Ibn Jurayj mentioned, Sufyān informed me from Rabīʿah ibn Sayf from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, raised (to the Prophet), similar to it. al-Tirmidhī narrated through the route of Rabīʿah without mentioning martyrdom, and said: "Gharīb, and Rabīʿah did not hear from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr." al-Ṭabarānī and Abū Yaʿlā have connected it through the ḥadīth of Rabīʿah from ʿIyāḍ from Qubbat al-ʿUzzā from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, may God be pleased with them. It has another route narrated by Aḥmad, Isḥāq and al-Ṭabarānī through the narration of Baqiyyah: "Muʿāwiyah narrated to me from Saʿīd: I heard Abū Qabīl say: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr," similar to it. Abū Nuʿaym in al-Ḥilyah, in the biography of Ibn al-Munkadir, narrated it through ʿUmar ibn Mūsā ibn al-Wajīh from Jābir, with the wording: "Whoever dies on Friday or on the night of Friday is protected from the punishment of the grave, and comes on the Day of Resurrection bearing the seal of the martyrs."]]. And in the ḥadīth: "When it is Friday, the angels sit at the doors of the mosque [[His words "at the doors of the mosque" are perhaps "the mosques." In al-Khāzin: "When it is Friday, there are angels at every door of the mosques, writing..." etc. (ʿ)]] with scrolls of silver in their hands and pens of gold, writing down the first and then the first, according to their ranks" [[Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh through ʿAmr ibn Samurah from Saʿd ibn Ṭarīf from al-Aṣbagh ibn Nubātah from ʿAlī, and its chain is extremely weak. It is in the Ṣaḥīḥ from the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah without the phrase "with scrolls of silver and pens of gold."]]. In the days of the early generation, the roads at the time of dawn and after daybreak were filled with those who came early to the Jumu'ah, walking with lamps.

It is said: the first innovation introduced in Islam was abandoning early attendance at the Jumu'ah. From Ibn Masʿūd: he came early and saw three men had preceded him, so he was distressed and began to reproach himself, saying: "I see you as the fourth of four, and the fourth of four is not fortunate" [[Narrated by Ibn Mājah and al-Bazzār through al-Aʿmash from Ibrāhīm from ʿAlqamah who said: "I went out with ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd to the Jumu'ah, and he found three had preceded him," and he mentioned it. It does not contain "he was distressed and began to reproach himself," and adds: "I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: People will sit before God on the Day of Resurrection according to the measure of their going to the Friday gatherings." They differed about the transmitter from al-Aʿmash, though both agreed it is from the narration of ʿAbd al-Majīd ibn Abī Rawwād. In Ibn Mājah, Maʿmar is between them; in al-Bazzār, Marwān ibn Sālim is between them. Ibn Abī Ḥātim mentioned it in al-ʿIlal, narrating from ʿAbd al-Majīd from al-Thawrī from al-Aʿmash, and this is not sound from al-Thawrī.]]. According to Abū Ḥanīfah, may God be pleased with him, the Jumu'ah is not established except in a major city (miṣr jāmiʿ), based on the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "There is no Jumu'ah, no tashrīq, no fiṭr and no aḍḥā except in a major city" [[I have not seen it as a marfūʿ (attributed to the Prophet) report. Ibn Abī Shaybah narrated it from ʿAlī, and its chain is weak.]]. A major city is that in which the ḥudūd (prescribed punishments) are enforced and the rulings are implemented. Among its conditions is the imam or one who stands in his place, based on the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "Whoever abandons it, when there is a just or unjust imam... the ḥadīth" [[Ibn Mājah narrated it through ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-ʿAdawī from ʿAlī ibn Zayd ibn Juda'ān from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab from Jābir, who said: "The Messenger of God ﷺ addressed us and said: 'O people, repent to God before you die'," the ḥadīth at length, and in it this and other things. Ibn ʿAdī narrated it. He narrated from Wakīʿ that al-ʿAdawī used to fabricate ḥadīth. It has another route with Abū Yaʿlā through the narration of Faḍīl ibn Marzūq: "al-Walīd ibn Bukayr informed me from Nimr ibn ʿAlī from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab." Its chain is questionable.

He said: al-Ṭabarānī narrated it in al-Awsaṭ through the narration of Mūsā ibn ʿAṭiyyah al-Bāhilī from Faḍīl ibn Marzūq from ʿAṭiyyah from Abū Saʿīd.

He said: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥabīb alone narrated it from Mūsā ibn ʿAṭiyyah. He said: Asad ibn Mūsā and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ al-ʿIjlī narrated it from Faḍīl ibn Marzūq from al-Walīd ibn Bukayr from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-ʿAdawī from ʿAlī ibn Zayd from Saʿīd from Jābir.

I say: So the other narration returns to al-ʿAdawī. Ibn Ḥibbān said in al-Ḍuʿafā': Ibn Khuzaymah informed us, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ghazwān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān "narrates wonders." He also narrated in al-Ḍuʿafā' through the route of Khālid ibn ʿAbd al-Dāʾim: Nāfiʿ ibn Yazīd narrated to us from Zuhrah ibn Maʿbad from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab from Abū Hurayrah; and he gave the name as "Khālid ibn ʿAbd al-Dāyim." al-Dāraqutnī said in al-ʿIlal: "Zuhrah and ʿAlī differed about its soundness." Both are not established.]]. And his saying ﷺ: "Four things are for the rulers: the spoils, the alms, the ḥudūd, and the Friday gatherings" [[I have not seen it as marfūʿ.]]. If a man leads the prayer without the imam's permission, or the permission of one he has appointed, such as a judge or a chief of police, it is not permitted. If there is no seeking of permission, but they gather around one person who leads them in prayer, it is permitted, and it is valid with three persons besides the imam. According to al-Shāfiʿī it requires forty. The Jumu'ah is not obligatory for travelers, slaves, women, the sick, or the chronically disabled; nor for the blind according to Abū Ḥanīfah, nor for the old man who cannot walk except with a guide.

ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd and others read: "fa-im-ḍū" (then proceed). It is reported from ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, that he heard a man reading "fa-is'aw" (then hasten), and said: "Who taught you this?" He said: "Ubayy ibn Kaʿb." He said: "He keeps on reading the abrogated! Had it been fa-is'aw, I would have hastened until my cloak fell off." It is also said: the meaning of "al-sa'y" is intention, not running; and "al-sa'y" means action in any work. From this is His saying, exalted: "When he reached with him the striving (al-sa'y)" [37:102], and "that man has nothing but what he strives for (sa'ā)" [53:39]. From al-Ḥasan: "Striving is not on the feet, but on intentions and hearts."

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, may God have mercy on him, mentioned in his Muwaṭṭa' that ʿUmar heard the iqāmah while he was at al-Baqīʿ, so he hastened his walk. Muḥammad said: "This is not objectionable, so long as he does not exert himself to the point of hindering the remembrance of God, (i.e.) the khuṭbah and the prayer." Because God named the khuṭbah a remembrance of Him, Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him, said: if the preacher limits himself to an amount that is called a remembrance of God, such as saying "al-ḥamdu lillāh, subḥān Allāh," it is permitted. [[He said: Maḥmūd "used this as evidence for the position of Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him..." etc. Aḥmad said: There is no proof in it, for the Arabs name a thing by the name of part of what it includes, as the prayer was called at one time "Qur'ān," at another "sujūd," and at another "rukūʿ," because it includes these. Likewise, since the khuṭbah includes the remembrance of God, it was named by it; but it does not follow that everything it includes is so named. Especially since what is called a khuṭbah among the Arabs must exceed the amount Abū Ḥanīfah is satisfied with. Some of Mālik's companions said: its minimum is praising God, sending blessings upon His Prophet, warning, giving glad tidings, and reciting Qur'ān.]] And from ʿUthmān: he went up the pulpit and said: "al-ḥamdu lillāh," and was tongue-tied, so he said: "Abū Bakr and ʿUmar used to prepare a speech for this station, and you need an effective imam more than a fluent speaker. Sermons will come to you after this," and then he descended. That took place in the presence of the Companions, and no one objected to him. According to his two companions and al-Shāfiʿī, there must be speech that is called a khuṭbah. If you say: how can the remembrance of God be explained as the khuṭbah when it contains mention of other than God? [[Maḥmūd said: "If you say: how is the remembrance of God explained as the khuṭbah when it contains mention other than God? He answered that the mention of the Messenger of God, the Companions and the rightly-guided caliphs..." etc. Aḥmad said: supplication for a ruler whose obedience is obligatory is legislated in every case. It is transmitted from some of the early generation that he supplicated for an unjust ruler, and it was said to him: "Do you supplicate for him while he is unjust?" He said: "Yes, by God, I supplicate for him, for what God averts through his continuance is greater than what is averted through his removal," especially when that supplication is accompanied by a prayer for his righteousness, rectitude and success. And God is the Granter of success.]] I say: whatever mention of the Messenger of God ﷺ, praise of him, of his rightly-guided caliphs, of the pious believers, admonition and reminder, is in the category of the remembrance of God. As for other than that, such as the mention of tyrants, their titles, praising them and supplicating for them when they deserve the opposite, the mention of Satan is at many stages from the remembrance of God. And when one listening to the khuṭbah says to his companion "ṣah" (hush), he has spoken idly; so would not the preacher who exaggerates in that be idle? We seek refuge in God from the strangeness of Islam and the hardship of the times.

He intended the command to abandon what distracts from the remembrance of God among the worldly preoccupations. He singled out trade from among them because the Friday is a day on which people descend from their villages and deserts and head toward the city from every direction. At the time of their descent and gathering, when the markets become crowded with them, when the day has swelled (inṭafakha al-nahār) [[His words "when the day has swelled": i.e., risen high. His words "taḥarr": i.e., grow thirsty, or its heat intensifies. Cited from al-Ṣiḥāḥ. (ʿ)]] and the forenoon has risen and noon approaches, then trade becomes hot and buying and selling multiply. Since that time is the likely occasion for being distracted by trade from the remembrance of God and proceeding to the mosque, they were told: hasten to the trade of the Hereafter, leave the trade of this world, and strive toward the remembrance of God, than which nothing is more beneficial or more profitable; "and leave off trade," whose benefit is small and whose gain is near. If you say: if buying and selling at this time is ordered to be abandoned and is forbidden, is it then invalid? I say: The majority of scholars hold that this does not necessitate the invalidity of the sale. They said: since the sale was not forbidden in itself, but because of the distraction it causes from the obligation, it is like prayer on usurped land, a usurped garment, or wudū' with usurped water. Some people said it is invalid. Then what was forbidden to them after the completion of the prayer was lifted: dispersing and seeking profit, along with the exhortation to increase the remembrance of God, and that no trade or anything else should distract them from it, and that their aspirations in all their states and times be entrusted to it, not diverted from it, for their success and their triumph depend upon it. From Ibn ʿAbbās: they were not commanded to seek anything of this world; rather it refers to visiting the sick, attending funerals, and visiting a brother for God's sake. From al-Ḥasan and Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab: seeking knowledge. It is also said: voluntary prayer.

It is reported that some of the early generation, after the Jumu'ah, would occupy himself with some matter of this world, reflecting on this verse.

Then he set out on Friday intending Madīnah, and the Friday prayer overtook him among the Banū Sālim ibn ʿAwf in the bottom of a valley of theirs, so he delivered the khuṭbah and led the Jumu'ah prayer [[Narrated by Ibn Isḥāq in al-Maghāzī from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar from ʿUrwah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUwaym: "some of my people informed me, saying: the Messenger of God ﷺ arrived in Madīnah on Monday," and he mentioned it at length. al-Bayhaqī narrated it through him in al-Dalā'il.

Ibn Hishām mentioned it in his abridgment from Ibn Isḥāq without a chain.]]. And from some of them: God has refuted the claims of the Jews in three respects. They boasted that they were God's friends and beloved, so He refuted them in His saying "then wish for death, if you are truthful" [2:94]. They said they were the People of the Book while the Arabs had no book, so He likened them to a donkey carrying books [62:5]. And (they had) the Sabbath, and that the Muslims had nothing like it, so God prescribed the Jumu'ah for them. And from the Prophet ﷺ: "The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he was admitted to Paradise, on it he was sent down to earth, on it the Hour will come, and it is with God the Day of Increase (yawm al-mazīd)." And from him, peace be upon him: "Gabriel came to me with a white mirror in his palm and said: 'This is Friday, which your Lord presents to you, to be a festival for you and for your community after you. It is the chief of days with us, and we call it the Day of Increase in the Hereafter.'" [[Agreed upon, except for the phrase "and it is with God the Day of Increase." al-Bazzār and al-Ṭabarī narrated it through the chain of Jahḍam ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṭufayl from Abū Ṭaybah from ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmayr from Anas, at length. Its wording is "and we call it in the Hereafter," and this is the correct version. In al-Ṭabarī's narration in his tafsīr of Qāf: "Abū Ṭaybah narrated to me from Muʿāwiyah al-ʿAbsī from ʿUthmān." Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam al-Bannānī and ʿAnbasah ibn Saʿīd, both from ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmayr from Anas. The chain of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam is from Abū Yaʿlā. Ibn Abī Shaybah and Isḥāq narrated it from the narration of Layth ibn Abī Sulaym from ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmayr. al-Shāfiʿī narrated it with a weak chain: he said, "Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Yaḥyā informed me, Mūsā ibn ʿUbaydah narrated to me, Abū al-Azhar Muʿāwiyah ibn Isḥāq ibn Ṭalḥah narrated to me from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmayr that he heard Anas ibn Mālik say something similar." It has another route from Anas narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ, through Thābit ibn Thawbān from Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh from Anas. Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh said: "Muḥammad ibn Shuʿayb informed us, ʿUmar, the client of ʿAmrah, narrated to me from Anas." It has a witness from the ḥadīth of Ḥudhayfah, narrated by al-Bazzār through al-Qāsim ibn Muṭayyib from al-Aʿmash from Abū Wā'il from him.]]. And from him ﷺ: "God, exalted is He, has in every Friday six hundred thousand persons freed from the Fire" [[Narrated by Abū Yaʿlā, al-Bayhaqī in al-Shuʿab, Ibn ʿAdī and Ibn Ḥibbān through Azwar ibn Ghālib from Sulaymān al-Taymī from Thābit from Anas. Al-Azwar: al-Dāraqutnī said, "abandoned" (matrūk). Abū Yaʿlā narrated it through al-Muʿtamir ibn Nāfiʿ from ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿUmarī from Thābit, "Anas narrated to me." It was narrated by al-Bukhārī in al-Tārīkh in the biography of al-Muʿtamir. al-Dāraqutnī narrated it in al-Afrād through ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Zayd ibn Thābit.]]. And from Kaʿb: God has preferred among the cities Mecca, among the months Ramaḍān, and among the days Friday. He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever dies on Friday, God records for him the reward of a martyr and protects him from the trial of the grave" [[ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Ibn Jurayj informed us from a man, from Ibn Shihāb, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever dies on Friday or on the night of Friday, he is protected from the trial of the grave and the reward of a martyr is recorded for him." Abū Murrah said in al-Sunan: Ibn Jurayj mentioned, Sufyān informed me from Rabīʿah ibn Sayf from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, raised (to the Prophet), similar to it. al-Tirmidhī narrated through the route of Rabīʿah without mentioning martyrdom, and said: "Gharīb, and Rabīʿah did not hear from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr." al-Ṭabarānī and Abū Yaʿlā have connected it through the ḥadīth of Rabīʿah from ʿIyāḍ from Qubbat al-ʿUzzā from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, may God be pleased with them. It has another route narrated by Aḥmad, Isḥāq and al-Ṭabarānī through the narration of Baqiyyah: "Muʿāwiyah narrated to me from Saʿīd: I heard Abū Qabīl say: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr," similar to it. Abū Nuʿaym in al-Ḥilyah, in the biography of Ibn al-Munkadir, narrated it through ʿUmar ibn Mūsā ibn al-Wajīh from Jābir, with the wording: "Whoever dies on Friday or on the night of Friday is protected from the punishment of the grave, and comes on the Day of Resurrection bearing the seal of the martyrs."]]. And in the ḥadīth: "When it is Friday, the angels sit at the doors of the mosque [[His words "at the doors of the mosque" are perhaps "the mosques." In al-Khāzin: "When it is Friday, there are angels at every door of the mosques, writing..." etc. (ʿ)]] with scrolls of silver in their hands and pens of gold, writing down the first and then the first, according to their ranks" [[Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh through ʿAmr ibn Samurah from Saʿd ibn Ṭarīf from al-Aṣbagh ibn Nubātah from ʿAlī, and its chain is extremely weak. It is in the Ṣaḥīḥ from the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah without the phrase "with scrolls of silver and pens of gold."]]. In the days of the early generation, the roads at the time of dawn and after daybreak were filled with those who came early to the Jumu'ah, walking with lamps.

It is said: the first innovation introduced in Islam was abandoning early attendance at the Jumu'ah. From Ibn Masʿūd: he came early and saw three men had preceded him, so he was distressed and began to reproach himself, saying: "I see you as the fourth of four, and the fourth of four is not fortunate" [[Narrated by Ibn Mājah and al-Bazzār through al-Aʿmash from Ibrāhīm from ʿAlqamah who said: "I went out with ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd to the Jumu'ah, and he found three had preceded him," and he mentioned it. It does not contain "he was distressed and began to reproach himself," and adds: "I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: People will sit before God on the Day of Resurrection according to the measure of their going to the Friday gatherings." They differed about the transmitter from al-Aʿmash, though both agreed it is from the narration of ʿAbd al-Majīd ibn Abī Rawwād. In Ibn Mājah, Maʿmar is between them; in al-Bazzār, Marwān ibn Sālim is between them. Ibn Abī Ḥātim mentioned it in al-ʿIlal, narrating from ʿAbd al-Majīd from al-Thawrī from al-Aʿmash, and this is not sound from al-Thawrī.]]. According to Abū Ḥanīfah, may God be pleased with him, the Jumu'ah is not established except in a major city (miṣr jāmiʿ), based on the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "There is no Jumu'ah, no tashrīq, no fiṭr and no aḍḥā except in a major city" [[I have not seen it as a marfūʿ (attributed to the Prophet) report. Ibn Abī Shaybah narrated it from ʿAlī, and its chain is weak.]]. A major city is that in which the ḥudūd (prescribed punishments) are enforced and the rulings are implemented. Among its conditions is the imam or one who stands in his place, based on the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "Whoever abandons it, when there is a just or unjust imam... the ḥadīth" [[Ibn Mājah narrated it through ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-ʿAdawī from ʿAlī ibn Zayd ibn Juda'ān from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab from Jābir, who said: "The Messenger of God ﷺ addressed us and said: 'O people, repent to God before you die'," the ḥadīth at length, and in it this and other things. Ibn ʿAdī narrated it. He narrated from Wakīʿ that al-ʿAdawī used to fabricate ḥadīth. It has another route with Abū Yaʿlā through the narration of Faḍīl ibn Marzūq: "al-Walīd ibn Bukayr informed me from Nimr ibn ʿAlī from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab." Its chain is questionable.

He said: al-Ṭabarānī narrated it in al-Awsaṭ through the narration of Mūsā ibn ʿAṭiyyah al-Bāhilī from Faḍīl ibn Marzūq from ʿAṭiyyah from Abū Saʿīd.

He said: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥabīb alone narrated it from Mūsā ibn ʿAṭiyyah. He said: Asad ibn Mūsā and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ al-ʿIjlī narrated it from Faḍīl ibn Marzūq from al-Walīd ibn Bukayr from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-ʿAdawī from ʿAlī ibn Zayd from Saʿīd from Jābir.

I say: So the other narration returns to al-ʿAdawī. Ibn Ḥibbān said in al-Ḍuʿafā': Ibn Khuzaymah informed us, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ghazwān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān "narrates wonders." He also narrated in al-Ḍuʿafā' through the route of Khālid ibn ʿAbd al-Dāʾim: Nāfiʿ ibn Yazīd narrated to us from Zuhrah ibn Maʿbad from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab from Abū Hurayrah; and he gave the name as "Khālid ibn ʿAbd al-Dāyim." al-Dāraqutnī said in al-ʿIlal: "Zuhrah and ʿAlī differed about its soundness." Both are not established.]]. And his saying ﷺ: "Four things are for the rulers: the spoils, the alms, the ḥudūd, and the Friday gatherings" [[I have not seen it as marfūʿ.]]. If a man leads the prayer without the imam's permission, or the permission of one he has appointed, such as a judge or a chief of police, it is not permitted. If there is no seeking of permission, but they gather around one person who leads them in prayer, it is permitted, and it is valid with three persons besides the imam. According to al-Shāfiʿī it requires forty. The Jumu'ah is not obligatory for travelers, slaves, women, the sick, or the chronically disabled; nor for the blind according to Abū Ḥanīfah, nor for the old man who cannot walk except with a guide.

ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd and others read: "fa-im-ḍū" (then proceed). It is reported from ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, that he heard a man reading "fa-is'aw" (then hasten), and said: "Who taught you this?" He said: "Ubayy ibn Kaʿb." He said: "He keeps on reading the abrogated! Had it been fa-is'aw, I would have hastened until my cloak fell off." It is also said: the meaning of "al-sa'y" is intention, not running; and "al-sa'y" means action in any work. From this is His saying, exalted: "When he reached with him the striving (al-sa'y)" [37:102], and "that man has nothing but what he strives for (sa'ā)" [53:39]. From al-Ḥasan: "Striving is not on the feet, but on intentions and hearts."

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, may God have mercy on him, mentioned in his Muwaṭṭa' that ʿUmar heard the iqāmah while he was at al-Baqīʿ, so he hastened his walk. Muḥammad said: "This is not objectionable, so long as he does not exert himself to the point of hindering the remembrance of God, (i.e.) the khuṭbah and the prayer." Because God named the khuṭbah a remembrance of Him, Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him, said: if the preacher limits himself to an amount that is called a remembrance of God, such as saying "al-ḥamdu lillāh, subḥān Allāh," it is permitted. [[He said: Maḥmūd "used this as evidence for the position of Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him..." etc. Aḥmad said: There is no proof in it, for the Arabs name a thing by the name of part of what it includes, as the prayer was called at one time "Qur'ān," at another "sujūd," and at another "rukūʿ," because it includes these. Likewise, since the khuṭbah includes the remembrance of God, it was named by it; but it does not follow that everything it includes is so named. Especially since what is called a khuṭbah among the Arabs must exceed the amount Abū Ḥanīfah is satisfied with. Some of Mālik's companions said: its minimum is praising God, sending blessings upon His Prophet, warning, giving glad tidings, and reciting Qur'ān.]] And from ʿUthmān: he went up the pulpit and said: "al-ḥamdu lillāh," and was tongue-tied, so he said: "Abū Bakr and ʿUmar used to prepare a speech for this station, and you need an effective imam more than a fluent speaker. Sermons will come to you after this," and then he descended. That took place in the presence of the Companions, and no one objected to him. According to his two companions and al-Shāfiʿī, there must be speech that is called a khuṭbah. If you say: how can the remembrance of God be explained as the khuṭbah when it contains mention of other than God? [[Maḥmūd said: "If you say: how is the remembrance of God explained as the khuṭbah when it contains mention other than God? He answered that the mention of the Messenger of God, the Companions and the rightly-guided caliphs..." etc. Aḥmad said: supplication for a ruler whose obedience is obligatory is legislated in every case. It is transmitted from some of the early generation that he supplicated for an unjust ruler, and it was said to him: "Do you supplicate for him while he is unjust?" He said: "Yes, by God, I supplicate for him, for what God averts through his continuance is greater than what is averted through his removal," especially when that supplication is accompanied by a prayer for his righteousness, rectitude and success. And God is the Granter of success.]] I say: whatever mention of the Messenger of God ﷺ, praise of him, of his rightly-guided caliphs, of the pious believers, admonition and reminder, is in the category of the remembrance of God. As for other than that, such as the mention of tyrants, their titles, praising them and supplicating for them when they deserve the opposite, the mention of Satan is at many stages from the remembrance of God. And when one listening to the khuṭbah says to his companion "ṣah" (hush), he has spoken idly; so would not the preacher who exaggerates in that be idle? We seek refuge in God from the strangeness of Islam and the hardship of the times.

He intended the command to abandon what distracts from the remembrance of God among the worldly preoccupations. He singled out trade from among them because the Friday is a day on which people descend from their villages and deserts and head toward the city from every direction. At the time of their descent and gathering, when the markets become crowded with them, when the day has swelled (inṭafakha al-nahār) [[His words "when the day has swelled": i.e., risen high. His words "taḥarr": i.e., grow thirsty, or its heat intensifies. Cited from al-Ṣiḥāḥ. (ʿ)]] and the forenoon has risen and noon approaches, then trade becomes hot and buying and selling multiply. Since that time is the likely occasion for being distracted by trade from the remembrance of God and proceeding to the mosque, they were told: hasten to the trade of the Hereafter, leave the trade of this world, and strive toward the remembrance of God, than which nothing is more beneficial or more profitable; "and leave off trade," whose benefit is small and whose gain is near. If you say: if buying and selling at this time is ordered to be abandoned and is forbidden, is it then invalid? I say: The majority of scholars hold that this does not necessitate the invalidity of the sale. They said: since the sale was not forbidden in itself, but because of the distraction it causes from the obligation, it is like prayer on usurped land, a usurped garment, or wudū' with usurped water. Some people said it is invalid. Then what was forbidden to them after the completion of the prayer was lifted: dispersing and seeking profit, along with the exhortation to increase the remembrance of God, and that no trade or anything else should distract them from it, and that their aspirations in all their states and times be entrusted to it, not diverted from it, for their success and their triumph depend upon it. From Ibn ʿAbbās: they were not commanded to seek anything of this world; rather it refers to visiting the sick, attending funerals, and visiting a brother for God's sake. From al-Ḥasan and Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab: seeking knowledge. It is also said: voluntary prayer.

It is reported that some of the early generation, after the Jumu'ah, would occupy himself with some matter of this world, reflecting on this verse.

It is related that the people of Madina were struck by hunger and severe scarcity of goods. Dihya ibn Khalifa arrived with a trade caravan of Syrian olive oil while the Prophet ﷺ was delivering the sermon on Friday. They rose toward it, fearing they would be beaten to it, so only a few remained with him. It was said: eight, eleven, twelve, or forty. Then he (peace be upon him) said:

"By Him in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, if they had all gone out, Allah would have set the valley ablaze over them." [[Al-Wahidi related this from the exegetes. Al-Tha'labi and then al-Baghawi related it from al-Hasan without a chain of narration. The wording of al-Hasan was recorded by ʿAbd al-Razzaq from Maʿmar from him, who said: "The people of Madina were struck by hunger and a high price of goods. A caravan arrived while the Prophet ﷺ was standing and delivering the sermon on Friday. They heard of it and went out toward it while the Prophet ﷺ was still standing and delivering the sermon as he was. So Allah the Exalted revealed: 'And they left you standing.' Then he said: 'If the last of them had followed the first of them, the valley would have been ablaze with fire over them.'" The version of Abu Sufyan, which comes later in Ibn Hibban, is similar. He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if you had followed one another until none of you remained, the valley would have flowed over you with fire." "This verse was revealed." The identification of Dihya in the phrase "they feared they would be beaten to it" was related by al-Tabari in abridged form from the narration of al-Suddi from Ibn Malik, who said: "Dihya ibn Khalifa arrived with a trade of raisins from Syria while the Prophet ﷺ was delivering the sermon on Friday. When they saw it, they rose, fearing they would be beaten to it, and the verse 'And when they see trade or amusement...' was revealed." Al-Bazzar related through ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was delivering the sermon on Friday when Dihya came to sell goods, and no one remained in the mosque except for a few men, while the Prophet ﷺ was standing, and then the verse was revealed." The origin of this story is in the two Sahihs, through Husayn from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd from Jabir, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was delivering the sermon standing on Friday when a caravan came from Syria, and the people dispersed until only twelve men remained, and then it was revealed." In the wording of Muslim: "among them Abu Bakr and ʿUmar." In another narration of his: "I was among them." In the narration of al-Bukhari: "While we were praying with the Prophet ﷺ, a caravan came." Al-Bayhaqi said: "The meaning of his saying 'pray' is 'listen to the sermon,' reconciling the two narrations, end quote." Ibn Hibban also recorded it through Abu Sufyan from Jabir in the same way, and his wording was: "While the Prophet ﷺ was delivering the sermon on Friday, a caravan came from Syria to Madina, and the companions of the Prophet ﷺ hastened to it until only twelve men remained with him... the hadith." It is corroborated by the hadith of Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra in Muslim, that he objected to ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Umm al-Hakam delivering the sermon while seated, saying: "Look at this man delivering the sermon while seated, when Allah says: 'And they left you standing.'" It also indicates that there was a sermon, as related by Abu Dawud in al-Marasil through Bakr ibn Maʿruf from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray on Friday before the sermon, until one day he was delivering the sermon after having prayed the Friday prayer, when a man entered and said: 'Dihya has arrived.' Whenever he arrived, they would welcome him with tambourines, so the people went out, not thinking that there was anything wrong with leaving the sermon, and Allah revealed the verse." So the Prophet ﷺ advanced the sermon on Friday and delayed the prayer. [Note: I have not come across a report that they were eight or eleven; the report of twelve is the well-known and sound one. The report of forty was recorded by al-Daraqutni through ʿAli ibn ʿAsim from Husayn, and he said: "None of Husayn's companions said forty except ʿAli ibn ʿAsim, and all of them said twelve men." Likewise Abu Sufyan related from Jabir, as mentioned earlier in Ibn Hibban.]] "a valley..." Whenever a caravan came, they would receive it with drums and clapping, and this is what is meant by "amusement." From Qatada: they did this three times with every arrival of a caravan. If you ask: what should be done if the people disperse from the imam during the Friday prayer? I say: if he remains alone or with fewer than three, then according to Abu Hanifa, he must begin the noon prayer anew if they leave him before bowing. According to his two companions, if he has pronounced the takbir while they were with him, he continues with it. According to Zufar, if they leave before the tashahhud, it is void. If you ask: how can it say "to it" when it mentioned two things? I say: the implied meaning is, if they saw trade they dispersed toward it, or amusement they dispersed toward it, so one of them was omitted because the mentioned one indicates it. Likewise is the reading of the one who reads "they dispersed to it" (anfaḍū ilayhi), and the reading of the one who reads "trade or amusement they dispersed toward them" (anfaḍū ilayhā). It is also read "to both of them" (ilayhimā).

From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Whoever recites Surah al-Jumu'ah will be given the reward of ten good deeds, equal to the number of those who attended Friday prayer and those who did not attend it, in the cities of the Muslims." [[Recorded by al-Tha'labi, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Wahidi with their chains to Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him.]]
